item.title: China, EU hold 17th economic, financial dialogue in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
China, EU hold 17th economic, financial dialogue in Beijing BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 17th China-EU Economic and Financial Dialogue was held in Beijing on Monday, with both sides discussing macroeconomic conditions and policies, as well as China-EU multilateral cooperation within the G20. China's Vice Minister of Finance Liao Min, who co-chaired the dialogue, said that under the current circumstances, China and the EU should jointly uphold and practice true multilateralism and work toward an open world economy to inject greater stability and certainty into the global economy. Major economies, including China and the EU, should take necessary measures to advance structural reforms, deepen macroeconomic policy coordination, keep global industrial and supply chains stable and smooth, and promote global economic and financial stability, Liao said. China is ready to expand mutual openness with the EU and make the cooperation pie bigger, Liao added, calling on the EU side to respect market economy principles and fair competition, and provide a fair, just and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese enterprises. Noting that the China-EU Economic and Financial Dialogue is an important platform for the two sides to deepen macroeconomic policy coordination and strengthen financial and economic cooperation, the EU side said it values macroeconomic policy communication and practical cooperation with China. The EU side said it is willing to strengthen constructive dialogue with China on the basis of mutual respect and reciprocal openness, carry out equal and mutually beneficial cooperation, properly address differences and disagreements, and advance the rebalancing of EU-China economic relations in an orderly manner. item.title: Power use surges in China's EV charging, data service sectors in October
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Power use surges in China's EV charging, data service sectors in October BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- Electricity consumption by China's electric vehicle charging and internet data service sectors soared in October, highlighting robust demand from the country's fast-growing new-energy vehicle and digital industries, official data showed Monday. Power consumption by charging and battery-swapping services reached 18.6 billion kilowatt-hours in October, surging 59.4 percent year on year, while that of internet data services jumped 34.7 percent to 9.9 billion kilowatt-hours, according to the National Energy Administration. NEVs accounted for 64.3 percent of new car sales last month, up from 61.6 percent in September, while the cumulative share for the first 10 months climbed to 54.8 percent, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. China's total electricity consumption for October stood at 870.9 billion kilowatt-hours, an increase of 1.6 percent year on year. Driven by rapid growth in electricity consumption by new business forms, power use in the tertiary industry grew the fastest among all industries, said Wu Liqiang, an official with the China Electricity Council. Electricity consumption by the tertiary industry rose 6.3 percent year on year to 171.4 billion kilowatt-hours in October. Electricity consumption by the primary industry stood at 12.4 billion kilowatt-hours, up 3.3 percent year on year, while power use by the secondary industry edged up 1.8 percent to 579 billion kilowatt-hours. Notably, power consumption by high-tech and equipment manufacturing industries climbed 6.5 percent year on year to 111.1 billion kilowatt-hours in October. In October, power use in high energy-consuming manufacturing sector posted negative year-on-year growth for three consecutive months, said Wu. In the first 10 months of 2026, China's total electricity consumption rose 3.7 percent year on year to 8.94 trillion kilowatt-hours. Electricity use by charging and battery-swapping services surged 55.9 percent in this period, while that of internet data services increased by 40.8 percent. According to an annual development report on China's electric power industry released by the China Electricity Council in July, total electricity consumption nationwide in 2026 is expected to increase by 5 percent to 6 percent year on year. item.title: Why is Europe's tech spotlight brightening with Chinese innovations?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Why is Europe's tech spotlight brightening with Chinese innovations? Chinese humanoid robots perform at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. (Photo/websummit.com) At Web Summit 2026 recently held in Lisbon, Portugal, performances by humanoid robots from China stole the spotlight. Clips quickly gained traction on social media, giving overseas netizens a closer look at the appeal of Chinese technology. At the opening ceremony, Web Summit CEO and founder Paddy Cosgrave said that future technology superstars would increasingly come from China. At a premier global tech gathering hosted in Europe, why did Chinese tech elements keep standing out, and why was China's presence growing more prominent? China's strong innovation capabilities are the most direct explanation. Chinese companies including Tencent, Xiaomi, Unitree Robotics, and Pony.ai, participated in this year's summit, showcasing breakthroughs across frontier fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), embodied AI, and autonomous driving. At the event, which brought together roughly 70,000 technology professionals, entrepreneurs and investors from around the world, Chinese innovations captured the attention of global industry players, thanks to solid technological foundations and competitive products. The growing attention to Chinese innovation also reflects a subtle shift in the global innovation landscape. This year's opening ceremony featured a dedicated frontier technology showcase. Chinese companies were invited to present solutions such as humanoid robots and flying cars, painting a picture of everyday life in the future for European audiences. Staff members collect data in a range of scenarios at an embodied AI robot data collection and training center in Suqian, east China's Jiangsu province. (Photo/Wang Shuaifu) For years, Silicon Valley and Europe's established research hubs were synonymous with global innovation centers. Today, when Europe looks for a tangible glimpse of tomorrow, its gaze is turning proactively toward China. That marks a shift in how the international community views China's role in innovation. Looking deeper, the rising prominence of Chinese innovations in Europe reflects not only shared needs, but also the inevitable logic of industrial development. Europe is home to many top universities and long-standing prowess in basic research and high-end manufacturing, yet faces bottlenecks in commercializing innovation. These include an underdeveloped digital platform ecosystem, limited cloud computing capacity, and slower AI commercialization. Bridging the "last mile" from lab breakthroughs to market application remains a persistent challenge for European industry. China's innovation drive has charted a differentiated path. By leveraging a massive engineering workforce, a complete industrial chain, and vast application scenarios, new technologies can rapidly complete a closed-loop iteration from laboratory to production line to real-world applications. Robots do more than perform on stage. They help in warehouses and retail stores. AI goes beyond conversations. It cuts costs and raises efficiency in industrial settings. What truly resonates in Europe is the substantial application potential and win-win business opportunities behind these innovations. Still, discordant voices persist. Even as growing numbers of business leaders and researchers recognize China as an indispensable force on the global innovation landscape, some European politicians remain conflicted about Chinese technology. They repeatedly hype the "de-risking" narrative and erect barriers in an attempt to restrict China-Europe cooperation on the sci-tech front. Yet such moves have neither changed the stance of the business and tech communities nor halted the endogenous drive for bilateral cooperation. Sci-tech cooperation between China and Europe is inherently built on complementary strengths. Europe's basic research and talent pool complement China's engineering capabilities and application testing. They are closely aligned in such fields as AI, green technology, and smart manufacturing. Foreign visitors watch a performance by a humanoid robot and a quadruped robot dog at a direct-operated store of Unitree Robotics on Wangfujing pedestrian street in Beijing. (Photo/Guo Junfeng) European enterprises can draw on Chinese solutions to accelerate digital transformation, while Chinese innovation entities can leverage European resources to enhance their technologies. This model of mutual empowerment has a solid foundation and enjoys broad room to grow. Sci-tech innovation is not a zero-sum game, and pursuing technological self-reliance is by no means synonymous with self-isolation. Choosing diverse technology supply and broad collaborative networks gives industrial development greater resilience. Equating competition with a threat or dismissing pragmatic cooperation as dependence only limits oneself and hinders future growth. When Europe's tech community looks toward China, it sees not only today's technological achievements, but a future of cooperation. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Experts warn against protectionism, call for pragmatic China-EU engagement
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Experts warn against protectionism, call for pragmatic China-EU engagement BELGRADE, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- European and Chinese experts on Monday called for a more pragmatic approach to China-Europe relations and stronger multilateral cooperation, warning that trade protectionism could hurt European consumers and undermine investment. The remarks were made at a panel discussion on the future of China-Europe relations hosted by the Belgrade-based Center for International Relations and Sustainable Development (CIRSD). Under the theme "De-Risking the Win-Win? The Trillion-Euro Question," the discussion explored how China and Europe could maintain mutually beneficial economic cooperation amid growing trade tensions and geopolitical uncertainties. Discussing recent trade arrangements between China and the EU concerning hybrid vehicles, Rudiger Frank, professor of East Asian economy and society at the University of Vienna, warned of the broader economic consequences of trade restrictions. He said artificially higher consumer prices could fuel inflation, push up interest rates, increase borrowing costs and discourage investment, creating a "vicious cycle" for the European economy. Frank advocated a multilateral approach to addressing trade imbalances, citing the WTO as an existing institutional framework and arguing that countries should seek an overall trade balance rather than balanced trade with each individual partner. Zhou Bo, a senior fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University, called on both China and Europe to set aside prejudices, adopt a realistic and pragmatic approach, and seek common ground for cooperation. Vuk Jeremic, president of CIRSD and former president of the United Nations General Assembly, who moderated the discussion, said closer cooperation with China could contribute to Europe's efforts to achieve strategic autonomy and economic prosperity. Jeremic said Europe needs to increase productivity and regain competitiveness, goals that could be advanced through closer, albeit careful, engagement with China rather than isolating itself from a major global economy and industrial and technological powerhouse. He said Europe should find ways to leverage its already substantial economic ties with China, addressing risks where necessary without sacrificing the potential of bilateral cooperation. item.title: China unveils Shenzhou-24 crew for space station mission, including first foreign astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
China unveils Shenzhou-24 crew for space station mission, including first foreign astronaut This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. (Xinhua) JIUQUAN, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, with Tang serving as commander, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. The three astronauts are a spacecraft pilot, a flight engineer and a payload specialist, respectively. Tang has participated in the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 crewed flight missions and is about to become the first astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station three times. Wu comes from the country's third batch of astronauts and will embark on his first spaceflight mission. Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Zhang Jingbo, spokesperson of the agency, said at a press conference. item.title: China's investment in new-type power grids expected to exceed 5 trillion yuan: What makes them different?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
China's investment in new-type power grids expected to exceed 5 trillion yuan: What makes them different? China has built the world's largest power supply system. In the first nine months of this year, the country's total electricity consumption surpassed 8.07 trillion kilowatt-hours, up 3.9 percent year on year. Meanwhile, China's power system is undergoing a series of changes on both the supply and demand sides. New energy is playing an increasingly prominent role in China's power mix, but it also brings greater volatility and uncertainty to the power grid. At the same time, the continued growth of emerging industries is creating higher demands for power quality. Photo shows a photovoltaic power station on Tunbashan Mountain in Mengshan county, Wuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region. (Photo/Wu Guangsheng) A meeting of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee held on April 28, 2026, called for efforts to step up the planning and construction of water networks, new-type power grids, computing infrastructure, new-generation communications networks, urban underground pipelines, and logistics systems. The development of new-type power grids has thus been incorporated into the country's top-level design. A robust power grid is essential to ensuring an adequate, safe, and reliable electricity supply. How is China advancing the rollout of these systems? "Compared with traditional power grids, building new-type power grids demands greater systems thinking. It should be rooted in regional resource endowments, industrial structures, load characteristics and distribution, while coordinating planning with the territorial spatial layout across time and space. This will enable the optimal allocation of energy resources across regions on a larger scale," said Yan Xiaoqing, director of the energy strategy research office of the energy institute under the State Grid Energy Research Institute Co., Ltd. A power grid consists of a backbone transmission network, distribution networks and smart microgrids, much like a three-tier road network of expressways, urban and rural roads, and neighborhood streets, Yan explained. The key to developing new-type power grids is to optimize this new grid architecture, Yan said, noting that the effective coordination among the main grid, distribution networks and microgrids levels provides reliable electricity support for the energy transition and high-quality development. "During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), investment in China's new-type power grids is expected to exceed 5 trillion yuan (about $749.87 billion). 15 additional ultra-high-voltage direct-current (UHVDC) transmission links are expected to be commissioned. Efforts will also be made to upgrade distribution networks through digital and intelligent technologies and accelerate the development of smart microgrids," said Yang Zhengang, senior manager of the planning management division of China Southern Power Grid's planning department. If the new architecture provides the framework, new technologies serve as its supporting tools. New energy storage systems: A "stabilizer" for power grids Photo shows an energy storage project in Pinglu county, Yuncheng, north China's Shanxi province. (Photo/Quan Yongjun) In Huangjiabu township, Yuyao, Ningbo, east China's Zhejiang province, 49 white energy storage containers stand in rows across the site of a 50-megawatt/100-megawatt-hour independent energy storage power station operated by a new energy company based in Ningbo. Inside the containers, different battery technologies serve distinct purposes. Lithium iron phosphate batteries on the eastern side offer large storage capacity and are used for peak shaving and valley filling, while lithium titanate batteries in the northwest respond more rapidly and are designed to address fluctuations in grid frequency. When the grid experiences fluctuations, the latter can adjust their power output within tens of milliseconds, compared with about 30 seconds for conventional thermal power units. Ningbo was the first city in China to surpass 10 million kilowatts of installed distributed photovoltaic (PV) capacity. But PV power generation depends on weather conditions: even a passing cloud can cause sharp fluctuations in output. From peak shaving and valley filling to rapid power response, new energy storage systems help ensure that fluctuating green electricity can not only be generated but also used reliably. They effectively serve as a readily available "power bank" and "stabilizer" for the urban grid. Artificial intelligence: Turning fluctuations into predictability This year, the summer peak in electricity consumption arrived more than a month earlier than usual. In late May, "Tianxiang," an artificial intelligence (AI) large model developed by China Southern Power Grid for meteorological forecasting, accurately identified the extreme heat expected in the second half of the month a week in advance. Another AI-powered load forecasting agent, "Tianyan," predicted electricity demand under high-temperature conditions 14 days ahead. It identified the prospect of high evening peak loads in south China's Guangdong province and a sharp decline in renewable energy output in southwest China's Yunnan province, helping power dispatch authorities prepare for the challenges posed by extreme heat. From forecasting and simulation to planning and inspection, AI is increasingly being integrated into every aspect of power grid operations. AI represents one of the most important technological directions for new-type power grids, said Xiao Liang, a technical expert at the dispatching and control center of China Southern Power Grid. AI helps optimize the allocation of grid resources and ensure the security of electricity supply, according to Xiao. New services: Making power supply more flexible A robotic dog conducts an inspection at a substation in Daxi township, Wenling, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/Xu Weijie) Ultimately, upgrades to grid architecture and technology are aimed at improving services. In Shenzhen, a "power plant" without a physical facility -- a virtual power plant -- is providing a new form of electricity service to the city. "As a new model in the power sector, the virtual power plant creates a pool of resources that can be flexibly coordinated. It brings together distributed and adjustable resources, including charging piles, building air-conditioning systems, and distributed energy storage facilities, and deeply integrates them with AI technologies to participate in power grid regulation," said Li Jiangnan, senior manager of the virtual power plant's management center. The center's management platform has connected 61 operators and more than 14,000 users, aggregating over 1.4 million kilowatts of real-time adjustable load capacity, equivalent to that of a medium-sized coal-fired power plant, Li said. The development of new-type power grids represents a profound transformation in grid architecture, technologies, and services, requiring coordinated planning and systematic measures. Tan Hongjiang, deputy director of the electricity department of China's National Energy Administration, said the administration would continue to advance the development of new-type power grids by optimizing new grid architecture, making breakthroughs in key new technologies, upgrading new power grid services, and stepping up efforts to advance the implementation of major tasks and projects. Astronauts of China's Shenzhou-24 mission meet press Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R) and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, for the upcoming Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission, meet the press at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Minggang) JIUQUAN, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, for the upcoming Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission, met the press on Tuesday. The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, the China Manned Space Agency announced at a press conference earlier Tuesday. item.title: Xi extends congratulations on Int'l Day of Solidarity with Palestinian People
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Xi extends congratulations on Int'l Day of Solidarity with Palestinian People BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping extended congratulations to a UN meeting held on Monday to commemorate the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People. In his message, Xi said that the Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue, adding that the current tensions in the Middle East should not divert the international community's attention from the Palestinian issue. The key to resolving the Palestinian question is to stay on course toward the two-state solution and promote the resumption of peace talks between Palestine and Israel, Xi said. He stressed that the governance of the West Bank and post-war reconstruction in Gaza should be advanced in accordance with the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine," and opposed any land-grabbing or rights-infringing actions targeting the Palestinian people. The international community should translate its consensus and commitments in support of Palestine into concrete actions, promote a lasting ceasefire in Gaza and protect the safety of civilians, Xi said. Xi said that justice will prevail and must not be absent. China has always firmly supported the just cause of the Palestinian people to restore their legitimate national rights, he said. China will continue to work with all countries that cherish peace and uphold justice to promote the early realization of a comprehensive, just and lasting solution of the Palestinian question, based on the rule of international law and with a view to addressing both its symptoms and root causes, Xi said. Such efforts will contribute to lasting peace and stability in the Middle East and make positive contributions to world peace, stability, development and prosperity, Xi added.
